migration_or_database_evidence: private.idempotency_records NOW EXISTS with couranr_begin_idempotent and couranr_complete_idempotent. Built in `private`, whose default ACL grants service_role only - `public` grants arwdDxtm to anon AND authenticated, so the same table there would be world-writable the instant it existed. couranr_payment_access_tokens exists (guest tokens); the five per-table idempotency_key unique indexes are deliberately NOT migrated - five incompatible scopes on live rows.

Also I11 (two system rows with actor_id NULL DO collide, so the coalesce in the unique index earns its place) and I16-I18 (three CHECKs that only fire on write).
remaining_work: Guest tokens remain. The message-write half is closed: a scoped UNIQUE on (conversation_id, author_participant_id, idempotency_key) plus couranr_conversation_events with a value-capped allow-list CHECK. The GENERAL-PURPOSE idempotency table now EXISTS and is executed 25/25, but is NOT YET WIRED to a caller: couranr_create_payment_obligation and couranr_begin_payment_capture are the two intended sites and are untouched, so the payment and webhook writes where resilientUpdateById still retries by dropping columns are not yet covered. Also open: the RETENTION WINDOW, which is an owner decision - expires_at is caller-supplied and NOT NULL precisely so no default invents one, and there is no purge job for the same reason.
notes: Idempotency is per-command today, not a platform primitive.
